problem:
Consider the differential equation ${y}^{″}+36{\pi }^{2}y=f(x),$ where the $1$-periodic forcing function is given by 

$$
f(x)∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{{n}^{2}}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2n\pi x).
$$

Select the correct options in the reasoning below regarding the resonant component of a particular solution of the equation.

The natural frequency of the system matches the frequency of the {{field-1}} harmonic of the forcing function.

feedback.problem:
Consider the differential equation ${y}^{″}+\frac{4{\pi }^{2}}{9}y=f(x),$ where the $6$-periodic forcing function is given by 

$$
f(x)∼-3+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{5}{{n}^{2}}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3}).
$$

Select the correct options in the reasoning below regarding the resonant component of a particular solution of the equation.

The natural frequency of the system matches the frequency of the {{field-1}} harmonic of the forcing function. 

Consequently, the particular solution contains a resonant term of the form

$$
{y}_{{p}_{2}}={{field-2}}.
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
We begin by identifying resonance. The differential equation 

$$
{y}^{″}+\frac{4{\pi }^{2}}{9}y=f(x)
$$

has a natural frequency of 

$$
\omega =\sqrt{\frac{4{\pi }^{2}}{9}}=\frac{2\pi }{3}.
$$

The frequencies of the forcing harmonics for a $6$-periodic function $(L=3)$ are 

$$
{\omega }_{n}=\frac{n\pi }{3}.
$$

For $n=2$, we have ${\omega }_{2}=\frac{2\pi }{3}.$ Since ${\omega }_{2}=\omega ,$ the $n=2$ harmonic of the forcing function causes resonance.

For the $n=2$ harmonic, the forcing term is 

$$
{f}_{2}(x)=\frac{5}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{2\pi x}{3}).
$$

Because this frequency matches the natural frequency, we assume a particular solution of the form

$$
{y}_{{p}_{2}}=x(A\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{2\pi x}{3})+B\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{2\pi x}{3})).
$$

Now, we compute the derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,{y}_{{p}_{2}}^{′} & =(A\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{2\pi x}{3})+B\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{2\pi x}{3}))+x(-\frac{2\pi }{3}A\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{2\pi x}{3})+\frac{2\pi }{3}B\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{2\pi x}{3})) \\ \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,{y}_{{p}_{2}}^{″} & =-\frac{4\pi }{3}A\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{2\pi x}{3})+\frac{4\pi }{3}B\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{2\pi x}{3})-\frac{4{\pi }^{2}}{9}x(A\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{2\pi x}{3})+B\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{2\pi x}{3}))\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the expressions for ${y}_{{p}_{2}}^{″}$ and ${y}_{{p}_{2}}$ into the equation ${y}^{″}+\frac{4{\pi }^{2}}{9}y=\frac{5}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{2\pi x}{3}):$

$$
[-\frac{4\pi }{3}A\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{2\pi x}{3})+\frac{4\pi }{3}B\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{2\pi x}{3})-\frac{4{\pi }^{2}}{9}{y}_{{p}_{2}}]+\frac{4{\pi }^{2}}{9}{y}_{{p}_{2}}=\frac{5}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{2\pi x}{3})
$$

The resonant terms involving $x$ cancel out, leaving

$$
-\frac{4\pi }{3}A\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{2\pi x}{3})+\frac{4\pi }{3}B\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{2\pi x}{3})=\frac{5}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{2\pi x}{3}).
$$

Now, equating the sine and cosine coefficients, we obtain:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-\frac{4\pi }{3}A=\frac{5}{4} \\ \frac{4\pi }{3}B=0\end{aligned}\,⇒\,{\begin{aligned}A=-\frac{15}{16\pi } \\ B=0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the resonant component of a particular solution is

$$
{y}_{{p}_{2}}=-\frac{15x}{16\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{2\pi x}{3}).
$$
